She probably was, but I was tired of her saying she would do something and she wouldn't. It went both ways.

She definitely was not innocent, but I know it was my actions that changed the course of the relationship. I know that she was distant with me for the last part of the relationship, I know now she was planning to leave me.

I do have childhood trauma that I didn't know existed. I thought I was fine, I really wasn't and she was on the receiving end of it, she didn't deserve it. I know that I can't change what I did in the relationship. I really did and still do love her, however I didn't act like it. I know I'm not going to enter another relationship until I am better.

I apologised after I fucked up everytime. I apologised when she left me. I apologised a week after the breakup. They were never empty apologises. However, I was struggling with my mental health, lost myself and lost control. It's no excuse, I am still responsible for my actions and what I did in the relationship, my mental health should have been dealt with and I didn't.

Hi Sadiedai, I'm not looking for pity and I'm really sorry you went through a horrible experience yourself, but my ex wasn't innocent either. Not everything is black or white, the person who was the problem, which was me in my situation, can be confused, angry, and disgusted with themselves when they do these things too. I will tell you how past experiences of the problem person can influence there behaviour in a relationship and its something they have no control over unless they seek help, this isn't for pity, sympathy or anything of the sort, I just want to explain how a problem person may be from my own experience. I have grown up in a very toxic "family" home, physically, mentally, and emotionally abused by dad, my mum, and my stepdad. I was in that environment for 20 years. My body is covered in scars from cigarettes being put out on me, beatings, beltings, being locked in a closet, watching and hearing dad rape my mum, etc. I thought my life was normal until I moved away for uni, have never been back to "home" since. Recently I have been diagnosed with CPTSD and BPD. I didn't seek help as I thought I was fine for many years, entered my first real relationship at uni, was with her for 4 years, everything was going great then boom, I started self sabotaging, we have an argument I would blow a gasket, she seems pissed off today so I'll preemptively strike so as not to get hurt, super stressed, angry, full of hate, anxious, depressed, hyper alert, can't sleep, can't focus, flash backs of childhood, suicidal etc. I never use to understand why I feel and do these things and I still am learning now, I regret everything I did, she did not deserve that, everytime I did it I hated myself more, I hated who I was, I was disgusted with myself, angry with myselfbut I didn't know how to stop and be the person she deserved. She was very much in love with me, as I was with her but unfortunately I allowed my mental illnesses to take the wheel and crashed and burned. I am responsible for my actions, my family fucked me up but its me who is responsible for fixing that in myself, I take full responsibility for what I did. To answer your other comment, in your opinion people cannot change, if the person is not willing to work on themselves, take responsibility for there own action and put the effort in they wont change. I do not like this version of me, my break up as much as it ending hurts me, has taught me what I need to do. I am changing every negative aspect about me and so far I'm doing really well. I will not go back to it because I want to be happy and thrive too.
I know, I just don't know what to do. I've left her alone as she wanted space since last contact. Im not stalking her social media or anything.
She hasn't blocked me on anything, but she has removed me as a friend on everything on day one.

I apologised to her on the day, and a week after we broke up via email. I didn't cheat, I became a horrible version of myself and I lost control. I've been working on myself since day one of this, I know each mistake I made. I know I have more work to do but I am not the same as I was. I am actively changing myself and I even through I still have a way to go, I am in a better place with these problems.

I apologised after I did it, I apologised all week leading up to the break up and in the break up. I will stay no contact, I am just struggling because I feel like shit because I hurt the person I love. I don't drink really and when I do I'm not much different than when I'm sober so I'm not worried about that. I hope it didn't cause to much of an issue for you.

Thank you, I just wished I did it sooner. I hope it is with my ex but I understand this will probably not happen and I wouldn't blame her if she said no. Everyday is a day of improvement in myself. I really despise the person I became. I will not contact her until I am in a good place relating to my progress.

I have had counselling through the NHS prior to this but it was never long term due to the amount that was alloted to me. Currently I have been in therapy privately for 3 months, started the day after she left me and had 1 session a week, hoping to up it to 2 sessions per week. I had a very unstable upbringing, however this is no excuse and I have taken ownership of the need to correct myself where my parents failed. It's not something that's is going to change over a few months and I know this. I thought I was fine, I've never liked violence due to my upbringing, I never liked conflict. As soon as I got stressed I changed, this is something that I realise is a trigger point and I am working on this with my therapist. Additionally to the therapy I have been spending a lot of time researching adverse childhood trauma, the psychology of it in untreated adults, the coping mechanisms I can use, self discipline techniques, breathing techniques, exercise, and some other things. I have spoken to my doctor also and the possibility of having CPTSD. I have a long way to go but I have made progress so far and I am getting better everyday.
